propositions: test_contended_index_lock_cleared_during_backoff_succeeds fails sporadically on macOS py3.13 CI when runner is slow, due to a wall-clock timer releasing a lock that git legitimately owns mid-commit

the test plants a young index.lock and uses threading.Timer(0.4) to delete it, but on slow runners git's own real index.lock is created after the planted lock is removed, and the timer deletes git's lock mid-commit causing 'fatal: unable to write new index file'
force_reclaim=True in _with_index_lock_retry bypasses the age gate, so the planted young lock is removed on the first retry attempt, not held long enough to trigger the intended backoff behavior
the test's timer has no identity check to distinguish the planted lock from git's real lock, so it blindly unlinks whatever lock exists at t=0.4
replacing the wall-clock threading.Timer with gitutil._retry_probe (a deterministic alternative that fires after each retry attempt) prevents deletion of git's lock while preserving test intent
